systems.system: Neutrino (OSDI 2025, Huang & Wu, HKU)
systems.design: (a) 按 launch 网格定大小的 ndarray 型 map：thread 级布局 [#Grid,#Block,cap]，warp 级布局 [#Grid,#Warp,cap]（只有 warp leader 写）。每个线程/warp 有自己独立的段，不用 atomic，元数据（threadIdx/blockIdx）靠下标推出、不存。每次 launch 时 hook 驱动 cuMemAlloc+memset，kernel 跑完同步、DtoH 拷回、fwrite、free（OSDI §3.3 p.335、§4.1；repo cuda.c L524-560、L617-660）。cap 有两种：固定整数，或 'dynamic'（两遍计数）。dynamic 时先完整跑一遍插了 count+=size 计数探针的 kernel，计数器为 grid×block×8B，拷回 CPU 后取所有线程的最大值，所有线程统一按这个最大值分配（cuda.c L495-520、L514-515；probe/cuda.py L258、L283-302）。SAVE 只做 st.global 加指针前移，不检查 cap 边界（probe/cuda.py L542-569）。论文 §3.3 说可以扩展出 ring 和 hash 类型，但 repo 里 Map.type 只有 Literal['array']（common.py L26，commit 4a82cd2）。repo 根地址：https://github.com/open-neutrino/neutrino/blob/4a82cd22f474c31ac2fecfa174d381a19bb3f469/

measurements.what: 每次 launch 的探针 buffer 峰值 GMEM（最大额外显存），整模型 forward。block_sched = warp 级，每 warp 记 16B 的开始时间戳/耗时/SM id，cap=1；gmem_bytes/tensorop_count = thread 级，每线程 8B 计数，cap=1；memtrace(dmat) = thread 级，每次访存记 16B（clock+地址），cap=dynamic
measurements.result: 格式为 block_sched / gmem_bytes / memtrace，括号里是原程序显存。ResNet BS32：6.1MB / 98MB / 7.08GB（562MB，memtrace 是原程序的约 12.6 倍）。SD-v1-5 BS1：3.1MB / 50MB / 1.78GB（2.11GB）。Mamba-1.7B BS32：5.5MB / 88MB / 2.45GB（2.99GB）。Llama3-1B BS32：224KB / 3.5MB / 759MB（2.57GB）。Llama3-3B BS32：384KB / 6MB / 1.05GB（6.29GB）。Llama3-8B BS32：512KB / 8MB / 1.35GB（15.27GB）。Llama3-8B BS128：2MB / 32MB / 2.75GB（15.52GB）。Llama3-8B BS256：4MB / 64MB / 5.50GB（16.05GB）。数值是从柱状图标签读的。论文说 dmat 'mostly remains within the original memory usage'，但 ResNet 这一项超过原程序 12 倍。
measurements.source: OSDI'25 §6.3 'GMEM Usage in Model Profiling'，Figure 12（p.342），https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi25-huang-songlin.pdf；预印本 Fig.12 内容相同，https://open-neutrino.github.io/Neutrino-Preprint.pdf
measurements.workload_gpu: ResNet/SD/Mamba/Llama3 推理 forward。§6 只说平台是 A100 80GB 和 RTX4090 24GB，没有说这张图用的是哪块 GPU

measurements.what: per-warp 和 per-thread map 的显存比（由 Fig.12 推算）
measurements.result: 8 个工作负载里 gmem_bytes / block_sched 都正好约等于 16 倍（98/6.1、50/3.1、88/5.5、3.5MB/224KB、8MB/512KB、32/2、64/4）。理论值：thread 级 8B×32 线程 = 256B/warp，warp 级 16B/warp，256/16 = 16，与实测一致。显存随 batch（也就是 grid）线性增长：Llama3-8B 的 BS32→128→256 对应 gmem_bytes 8→32→64MB，memtrace 1.35→2.75→5.50GB。这两组探针记录的内容不同，所以这只是显存比较，不是同一个探针下的 A/B 实验。

measurements.what: kernel 减速（只看探针插桩后的 kernel 时间，不含 buffer 分配和拷回）。benchmark 模式：探针 kernel 和剥掉探针、用同样参数汇编的 pruned kernel 各计时一次（cuda.c L580-680）
measurements.result: 轻量探针（block_sched warp:array:16:1、gmem_bytes / tensorop_count thread:array:8:1）平均 1.04x，范围 0.9596x（Gather）到 1.3882x（Max/AvgPool, gmem_bytes）。重探针 mem_trace（thread:array:16:count）平均 7.12x，范围 2.7463x（Conv2D）到 13.1630x（SoftMax），例如 GEMM 8.8933x、Flash-Attn v2 2.9392x。额外寄存器：轻量探针平均 +3.78，dmat 平均 +5.09，Group-GEMM mem_trace +516（spill）。

measurements.what: 记录频率与减速的关系（dmat 按 1/8、1/4、1/3、1/2、全量采样）
measurements.result: 减速和采样率大致成线性。pool（3.69% 访存指令，约 5555 cycle/block）：约 2.5x（1/8）→ 约 13.5x（全量）。gemm（17.57% 访存，约 116531 cycle/block）：约 1.8x → 约 6.6x。attn（11.03% 访存，约 205101 cycle/block）：约 1.1x → 约 2.5x。数值从图上读，是近似值。作者结论是 'most DMAT cost comes from the I/O'。每次 save 包含读 clock、算地址、存 16B，所以这是每条记录的总成本，不是单纯写 buffer 的成本。

measurements.what: 对上层可见的总延迟分解：prologue（分配 map、调用 probe engine）+ kernel + epilogue（DtoH 拷回、写盘、free）
measurements.result: prologue < 1%。Neutrino 总量是原 kernel 时间的倍数，括号里是 'Other'（prologue+epilogue）部分，从图上读，近似：FlashAttnv2-Triton（BS=4, CTX=4096, H=32, D=64）block_sched 1.39x（约 0.1）、tensorop_count 2.38x（约 1.1）、gmem_bytes 2.56x（约 1.15）。Persist GroupMM-Triton block_sched 1.36x、tensorop 1.38x、gmem 1.42x（Other 都约 0.1）。Conv2D-CUTLASS（BS=256, H/W=56, C/K=128）block_sched 1.36x（约 0.3）、tensorop 5.45x（约 4.0）、gmem 5.32x（约 4.0）。GEMM-CUTLASS（4096³）block_sched 1.56x（约 0.3）、tensorop 2.97x（约 1.75）、gmem 2.98x（约 1.75）。结论：对大网格上的 thread 级 map，拷回加写盘（collection）占了大头，最多约 4 倍原 kernel 时间，比探针本身导致的 kernel 减速还大；warp 级的 block_sched 这部分很小。

systems.not_measured: 1) dynamic（两遍计数）的成本：多跑一次完整 kernel、grid×block×8B 计数器、DtoH 拷回、CPU 求 max。这些时间计入 prologue 计时窗口（cuda.c L322 到 L585），但 Fig.13 的三个探针都是固定 cap=1，Table 3 只比较探针 kernel 和 pruned kernel 的时间，所以计数遍的成本没有任何数字。代码注释 L486-493 写着：COUNT 对就地修改输入的 kernel 会出错（比如 topP/topK），这时要用足够大的常数；考虑过 ring buffer，没有实现。2) 统一按最大计数分配，线程之间负载不均时浪费多少显存。3) 超过 cap 的行为：SAVE 不做边界检查，越界会写进相邻线程的段甚至越出 buffer，属于静默损坏，不是丢弃。丢失或损坏率没有测过。4) 同一个探针在 per-thread 和 per-warp 两种 map 下的运行时开销，没有 A/B 对照。5) ring/hash map 没有实现，也没有测过。6) 线程数扩展只能间接从 batch 维度看到（Fig.12）；按事件率扩展只有 Fig.16。7) 和 atomic 共享 buffer 的直接对比：§3.3 只是定性地说 atomics 'can become inefficient'，没有数字。8) 和 NVBit channel、GT-Pin、CUPTI 的比较没有做；只和 Nsight Compute 比较了总延迟。

systems.system: Xtrace (arXiv 2609.28769v1, NUS + Meta, 2026-09)
systems.design: (a) 按 launch 规模定大小的 trace buffer，每个线程一个偏移 slot，slot 当作 ring buffer 用。INIT 探针在 kernel 入口把 buffer 地址和 ring 指针放进 3 个 32-bit 死寄存器；RECORD 探针写 (值, probe id) 后推进指针。kernel 结束后由驱动遍历各 slot 收集（§3、§4.5 p.8-9）。寄存器不够时会降级成 per-warp 寄存器和 per-warp 记录（§4.3）。评测中三个工具一律由一个选出的 lane 按 warp 记录（§5.1）。论文和文档都没有给出 slot 容量、写满时的语义（从 ring 推测是覆盖旧记录），也没有给出 buffer 大小的配置项。g-watch.github.io 的 Xtrace/CUDA 文档页也没有这些信息，源码没有找到公开仓库（以 pip 包形式发布）。

measurements.what: 端到端 kernel 时间开销，取各 trace 类型里最差的情况。trace-sche 只在 warp 进出各记一次，最轻；trace-pp 在每个流水级边界记时间戳；trace-mem 每次访存都记，最重

measurements.what: 写 trace 那条 store 的代价（这是最接近 '写 buffer 成本' 的数字）
measurements.result: Neutrino 的 FA-3 producer 探针里，PRMT 因为对 trace store 的 WAR 依赖，77% 的时间在等这条 store。consumer 端 SoftMax 首条指令有 13% 的等待来自 probe store 的 scoreboard。Hopper 上一次 global store 要 270-380ns，和被测区域的长度相当。另外 store 等待会让整个 warp 在汇合点停住，不只是写的那个线程。Xtrace 改用 per-SM clock：读取约 10ns，而 global timer 要数百 ns。

systems.not_measured: Xtrace 自己 trace buffer 的显存占用、slot 容量、ring 回绕导致的覆盖或丢失、和 per-thread 记录的比较（评测统一用 per-warp 记录，所以对 per-thread buffer 的成本什么都没说）、buffer 拷回和解析的时间。所有开销都归因到编译期干扰（binary similarity）和寄存器/scoreboard 依赖，buffer 设计没有被单独隔离出来。

systems.system: NVIDIA CuTeDSL IKET（数据来自 Xtrace 的测量，加上 NVIDIA 文档）
systems.design: 在源码层预留 placeholder，到二进制层再替换成探针。文档写明 trace buffer 按 warp 存、两遍分配：先跑一遍估算大小，再加余量分配。可以用 --max-ts-cnt-per-warp N 预留每 warp 最多 N 个事件。如果两遍之间每 warp 的记录数不同，'trace may contain incorrect data'。写满时的行为文档没有说。（https://docs.nvidia.com/cutlass/latest/media/docs/pythonDSL/guides/iket_profiling.html）

measurements.what: 端到端开销（Xtrace 用自己重新实现的 IKET 测，输出二进制与原版逐位一致）
measurements.result: 见 Xtrace 一栏：最差 3.8%（FA-3）、20.0%（FlashMLA）、28.4%（FA-4）；trace-pp 1.3-3.8%；trace-mem 0.5-28.4%。原版 IKET 的墙钟时间最多 +133%，但这个数包含运行时 patch 二进制的时间，不是 kernel 本身的开销。

systems.not_measured: 两遍 sizing 的时间成本、buffer 显存占用、超出预留量时的行为，都没有测。原版在最大的两个 FA-3 launch 上崩溃，原因没有说明，不能归因到 buffer 设计。

comparisons: Neutrino 内部 per-warp 和 per-thread 的显存对比：同一模型下 thread 级 8B/线程的 map 正好是 warp 级 16B/warp 的 16 倍（8 个工作负载都一致，例如 ResNet BS32 98MB 对 6.1MB），与 8×32/16 的理论值吻合。来源：OSDI'25 Figure 12 p.342。两组探针记录的内容不同，所以只能比较显存。

Neutrino 的收集成本（per-warp 对 per-thread，从 Figure 13 读，近似）：Conv2D-CUTLASS BS=256 上，thread 级 tensorop_count / gmem_bytes 总暴露延迟 5.45x / 5.32x，其中 prologue+epilogue（拷回加写盘）约 4.0x；warp 级 block_sched 总共 1.36x，Other 约 0.3x。这说明对大网格的 per-thread 数组，主要成本在收集，不在探针。来源：OSDI'25 Figure 13 p.342。

Neutrino 和 Nsight Compute 的对上层暴露延迟（倍数，Nsight 是 kernel replay，不是同类机制）：FlashAttnv2 2.31/5.69/4.76 对 1.39/2.38/2.56；Persist GroupMM 3.47/13.10/7.97 对 1.36/1.38/1.42；Conv2D 4.17/15.38/9.03 对 1.36/5.45/5.32；GEMM 7.34/15.47/18.22 对 1.56/2.97/2.98（顺序是 block_sched/tensorop_count/gmem_bytes）。来源：OSDI'25 Figure 13 p.342。

Xtrace、Neutrino、IKET 三者的端到端开销（最差 trace 类型）：FA-3 H100 2.7% / 11.8% / 3.8%，FlashMLA H100 0.9% / 36.9% / 20.0%，FA-4 B300 2.8% / 75.6% / 28.4%。三者都是按 launch 定大小、per-warp 记录，差别主要在插桩层次（二进制拼接、IR、placeholder），不是 buffer 设计。来源：arXiv 2609.28769 Figure 1b、§5.4.2。
随记录量扩展（Xtrace Figure 14）：CTA 从 32 增加到 2048、记录数增加 249 倍时，Xtrace ≤3.5%、Neutrino ≤13.9%、IKET ≤5.1%，曲线基本平。说明按 launch 预分配的 per-slot buffer 在记录量上升时没有额外退化；但没有测显存，也没有和共享 ring 或 atomic 方案比较。
notes:
范围：这次只看了分配给我的 Neutrino、Xtrace，以及 Xtrace 测到的 IKET（加上 NVIDIA IKET 文档）。设计 (b) NVBit channel / BPF ringbuf、(c) GT-Pin、(d) SASSI / gpu_ext、(e) CUPTI、(f) bpftime 都不在这次来源里，没有调研。

核心结论：
1) 两篇论文都没有设计过 buffer 设计之间的对照实验。Neutrino 是唯一给出显存数字（Fig.12）和收集延迟拆分（Fig.13）的；Xtrace 的所有比较都把开销归到编译干扰和寄存器/scoreboard 依赖，没有测 buffer 显存。
2) 对 bpftime 有参考价值的点：
 - per-warp 布局能把显存降 16 倍（在 thread 8B / warp 16B 的配置下）。
 - 对大网格的 per-thread 数组，拷回加写盘的时间可以达到原 kernel 的约 4 倍，比探针本身的开销还大。
 - 实际工作负载里动态计数得出的每线程记录数在几十条量级（推算 ResNet 约 36、Llama3-8B 约 84，需要谨慎看），远小于固定的 1024。
 - 两遍计数（Neutrino dynamic、IKET）都有正确性前提：kernel 不能就地修改输入，两遍之间的记录数要一致。两者的时间成本都没有人测过。
3) Neutrino 实现上的细节：SAVE 不检查 cap 边界，超出时是静默写坏邻近线程的段，不是丢弃；dynamic 统一按所有线程的最大计数分配；ring 和 hash 只在论文里提到，repo 里只有 array。
4) Neutrino 的 Table 3 / Fig.12 / Fig.13 没有标明用的是 A100 还是 RTX4090；Fig.13 的分段数值和 Fig.16 的曲线点是我从图上读的近似值。Xtrace Fig.1b 的数值已经放大核对过。
5) OSDI 正式版和预印本的 Table 3、Fig.12/13 内容一致。

systems.system: NVBit (NVIDIA, MICRO 2019; release v1.8.1, 2026-09-29)
systems.design: (b) One shared GPU->CPU channel per CUDA context. Producers reserve space with an atomic fetch_add on head_bytes, copy the packet, then advance tail_bytes. Buffer: 1 MiB (CHANNEL_SIZE 1<<20) of mapped pinned host memory by default. The mem_trace tool aggregates per warp: lanes exchange addresses with __shfl_sync and only the first active lane pushes one 288-byte mem_access_t (8 B launch id + 5 ints + 32x8 B addresses), so about 3,640 warp records fit per round. When full it BLOCKS and never drops: the producer that crosses the end waits for tail==curr, writes the byte count to a host-visible doorbell, and spins until the host thread drains and writes 0. Every other producer spins while head > buff_size. In effect the whole device stalls for each host drain. The paper's own example tools (Listing 1, Listing 8) are design (d): __managed__ counters updated with atomicAdd, plus warp-leader election.

measurements.what: Paper's qualitative statement on per-call cost
measurements.result: No number. Every active thread enters and leaves the instrumentation function, and saving registers before each call 'takes many cycles and can destroy cache locality'.

measurements.what: Channel buffer size and record size (code facts, not measurements)
measurements.result: 1 MiB per context (mem_trace.cu:72). 288 B per warp-level record (common.h, mem_access_t), so about 3,640 records per flush round. The host recv buffer is another 1 MiB malloc (mem_trace.cu:475).

measurements.what: Behaviour when the channel is full (code facts)
measurements.result: Blocks, never drops. Non-flushing producers spin while head>buff_size (core/utils/channel.hpp:124-128). The flusher waits for tail==nbytes, stores the doorbell, then spins until the host writes 0 (channel.hpp:196-205), resets (208-209). The buffer is cudaHostAlloc mapped by default, or device memory with USE_ASYNC_STREAM (channel.hpp:83-86, ~285-289). USE_ASYNC_STREAM is documented to deadlock when a CUDA API call holds the context lock while the kernel waits for its flush (mem_trace.cu:52-60). Warp aggregation: inject_funcs.cu:52-75.

systems.system: SASSI (NVIDIA, ISCA 2015)
systems.design: (d) Compiler-inserted (ptxas backend) calls to user CUDA handlers. systems.system: GT-Pin / GTPin (Intel)
systems.design: (c) A trace or profile buffer allocated by the tool, mapped to both CPU and GPU, and read by the CPU after the kernel or at sync points. API: GtProfileArray, where threads are hashed by thread ID into thread buckets. Each bucket writes its own non-interleaving chunk. Bucket count is a power of two in [1, max HW threads], 'to minimize contention of concurrent memory accesses'. GtProfileTrace is a chronological record trace: maxTraceSize in bytes, maxThreads default 0x1000. On overflow the trace is truncated (records dropped): IsTruncated() returns true and the generated code sets flag f0.0. Basic-block counting keeps the counter in a register and writes the final value to the buffer at program end (2015 paper).

systems.system: CUPTI (NVIDIA): PC sampling + Activity buffers
systems.design: (e) Hardware PC sampling. Each SM samples one warp scheduler every 2^N cycles (N in 5..31; the default depends on SM count) into a hardware buffer in device memory (default 512 MB). CUPTI copies it into a software scratch buffer (default 1 MB, about 5,500 PCs with all stall reasons, about 16 B per PC per stall reason). Samples are dropped on backpressure or overflow and reported in droppedSamples. When the HW buffer is full, hardwareBufferFull is set, CUPTI_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY is returned and PC data is 0. Activity tracing: device buffer 3,200,000 B (about 100,000 kernel/memcpy/memset records), pool limit 250 buffers per context. Records are dropped if the client gives no empty buffers, counted by cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords. HES buffer 128 MB, drops when full.

measurements.result: HW buffer 512 MB; scratch 1 MB (about 5,500 PCs); activity device buffer about 3 MB (about 100k records), pool 250; HES 128 MB. Drops are counted, not prevented.
measurements.source: CUDA 13.2 headers on this board: /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets/sbsa-linux/include/cupti_pcsampling.h:196-240 (totalSamples/droppedSamples/hardwareBufferFull), :277-296 (scratch 1 MB, HW 512 MB); cupti_activity.h:9885-9944 (device buffer 3,200,000 B, pool 250), :10748-10772 (dropped records). systems.system: compute-sanitizer MemoryTracker sample (NVIDIA compute-sanitizer-samples, commit 1e1fab8e, 2023-11-06)
systems.design: (b) with per-launch sizing, one record per thread-level access and no warp aggregation. At each launch (LaunchBegin) it does sanitizerAlloc of MEM_ACCESS_SIZE entries (default 1024) x 32-byte MemoryAccess = 32 KiB, plus a tracker {currentEntry, maxEntry}. The device callback reserves with a single atomicAdd(&currentEntry,1). If old >= maxEntry it returns SUCCESS and silently drops the record, but currentEntry keeps counting, so drops = currentEntry - maxEntry can be recovered. The host copies min(currentEntry,maxEntry) records at stream or context sync. There is no mid-kernel flush and no blocking.

systems.system: GVProf (Rice, SC'20), built on the NVIDIA Sanitizer API (third-party, same mechanism as MemoryTracker)
systems.design: (b) One GPU queue per CUDA stream, default 72 MB ('a good tradeoff between runtime and memory overhead from our experiments'). Operations are atomic. notes: The short answer to 'which of these were actually measured, and how did they do': all five assigned systems were measured only end to end, and no paper isolates the buffering design except SASSI's one stubbed-handler sentence. The NVBit paper never measures its channel. Its 36.4x/112x and 2.3x numbers (Fig. 8) are for a counter-style tool. The channel's blocking behaviour (device-wide spin while the host drains 1 MiB of pinned memory) is visible only from code (channel.hpp v1.8.1), and nobody has published channel throughput, stall time or mem_trace slowdown. CUPTI numbers are configured defaults and drop-counting semantics, not measurements. NVIDIA gives no drop rate or overhead percentage. The compute-sanitizer MemoryTracker sample has no measurements; it is a per-launch 32 KiB buffer that drops silently but keeps a recoverable overflow count. GT-Pin has only end-to-end figures: 2-10x (IISWC'15, HD 4000), 4.7x (XPU-Point, Max 1100), 1.81x to 2.23x (HPCToolkit, Iris Pro). Its bucket and truncation behaviour comes from the docs only. GVProf is a useful third-party Sanitizer-API data point for a blocking shared queue (72 MB, kernel paused when full). Overall gaps: (1) nobody measured scaling with thread count or grid size; (2) no paper sweeps buffer size against overhead or drops; (3) memory footprints are configured sizes, never measured peaks; (4) the partial isolations are SASSI's about 80/20 probe vs collection split (K40m), gpu_ext's per-thread vs warp-level (60-80% less) and PCIe-map (6000x) microbenchmarks, and the HPCToolkit coarse-to-fine delta. Items to watch: the gpu_ext text vs Table 2 mismatch (85-87% vs 93%); the HPCToolkit NVIDIA 2.24x does not say whether PC sampling was on; XPU-Point Fig. 16 values are eyeballed. I could not get the ISPASS'26 GTPin paper PDF (only its artifact repo). Neutrino, Xtrace and the gpu_ext design were treated as out of scope except for head-to-head numbers. systems.design: Closest to design (a), but sized from a profiling pass instead of from the grid. The kernel runs twice. A counters pass counts basic-block executions per producer. The host then computes each producer's exact event count E[Pi]=Ci·E and takes an exclusive-scan offset O[i] (thesis eq. 4.1/4.2, Fig. 4.1). A second, tracing pass writes into a preallocated 'parallel array' slice per producer with no atomics. Inputs are duplicated and restored between the passes. Producer is a wavefront (64 threads on AMD) by default. A per-thread mode exists but its overhead is never reported. A WaveState event is 24 B. Non-deterministic kernels can overflow their slice and overwrite other producers' events, so a '4x padding' variant exists.

systems.system: hip-analyzer online tracing schemes (Darche, Dagenais, Lamothe, 'Tracing Schemes for Performance Analysis of Compute Kernels on GPUs', submitted to ACM TOPC Nov 2024; thesis Ch. 5 and Ch. 6; code https://github.com/dorsal-lab/hip-analyzer)
systems.design: Four schemes run on the same instrumentation (WaveState event per basic block, one producer per 64-thread wavefront, constructors in hand-written GCN asm, tracing state in reserved SGPRs). (1) hip-global-mem (GlobalMemoryTrace) = design (b): one buffer per stream, one global atomic per event (n_a = n_e, eq. 5.1). (2) hip-cu-mem (CUMemoryTrace) = (b) sharded per CU: one buffer and atomic pointer per CU, chosen via the HW_ID register (like %smid on NVIDIA). (3) hip-chunk-allocator (ChunkAllocator) = (b) with chunk reservation: one atomic reserves a fixed-size sub-buffer, then the wavefront writes events with a register-held offset, so n_a = n_e·Ne/Nsb (eq. 5.2). (4) hip-cu-chunk-allocator = per-CU buffers plus chunks, with registries aligned to cache lines. Sizes are powers of two. The default is 2^20 sub-buffers of 4 KiB. Code: include/hip_instrumentation/managed_queue_info.hpp. Registry::alloc does atomicAdd(&current_id,1) then next=(next % buffer_count)*buffer_size, with no device-side full check (L111-121). TOTAL_CU_COUNT=112 and CACHE_LINE_SIZE=64 are hard-coded (L162-167). DEFAULT_SIZE=1048576 for GlobalMemoryQueueInfo/CUMemoryTrace (L148, L243; the code comment wrongly says '2 Mb'). When full, the buffer behaves as a flight recorder and overwrites old events. The host detects overwrites from the index delta at kernel end (§5.3.3). The host can only read buffers at kernel boundaries on CDNA2, so buffers must hold a whole kernel's events. A blocking mode is called impossible without deadlock or a costly host call (§5.5.2).

systems.system: PASTA (Lin, Jeon, Zhou; arXiv 2602.22103, Feb 2026, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.22103)
systems.design: The paper compares two designs. The baseline (its Fig. 2a) is the conventional design (b): GPU hooks write a device trace buffer, the GPU stalls when it is full, and the CPU fetches it, flushes it and analyzes it on one thread. This is how NVBit MemTrace and the Compute Sanitizer MemoryTracker work. PASTA (Fig. 2b) uses design (d): collection and analysis happen on the GPU (a per-object access-count map incremented on the device), with no per-event trace shipped to the host.

The 'GPU stalls when trace buffer is full' behaviour of the baseline is described (Fig. 2a), never timed. No buffer size, memory footprint, drop count or scaling-with-threads numbers. systems.system: CUDAAdvisor (Shen, Song, Li, Liu, CGO 2018, DOI 10.1145/3168831; code https://github.com/sderek/CUDAAdvisor)
systems.design: Design (b) in its simplest form. A single global device buffer (BUFFERSIZE = 24*80*1024*1024 B ≈ 1.97 GB, common.h L1). Each traced thread does atomicAdd on one global counter per event (src/ansf.cu L632 for basic-block logs, L695 for memory-access entries). Events are per-thread records (Entry_t: block/thread ids, address, size, line, op). When the counter nears capacity, the hook silently returns, i.e. drops the event (ansf.cu L633-634, L690-691). Optional sampling of CTAs (CTALB/CTAUB, L626-627) limits volume.

measurements.result: 10x to 120x, averaging about 50x on Rodinia (SECONDHAND: quoted in Darche thesis §2, about line 1238 of the text, and in Dorsal slides; Darche could not run CUDAAdvisor on its hardware)

No drop counts, although code drops silently on overflow. No memory-footprint study beyond the fixed ~2 GB buffer.

systems.design: Design (e): CUPTI PC sampling. Per the paper, each SM collects samples into a hardware/driver buffer. When it is full, CUPTI merges the samples from all SMs and transfers them to the CPU.
systems.not_measured: No overhead, buffer size, sample loss or scaling measurement for collection. The paper only claims PC sampling 'introduces considerably less cost' than instrumentation (related work). The 1.01x-3.53x (geomean 1.22x) numbers are application speedups after GPA's advice, not overhead (§2.1 and evaluation).

systems.design: Design (e) plus static analysis: CUPTI PC Sampling for warp stalls, Nsight Compute CLI for kernel metrics, and SASS static analysis. It has no instrumentation buffer of its own.

systems.system: KPerfIR / Proton intra-kernel profiler (Guan et al., arXiv 2505.21661, May 2025)
systems.design: Region timing for Triton kernels. Records go to a per-warp-group slice of a shared-memory buffer. Slot offsets are fixed at compile time, so writes need no atomics. A circular buffer keeps only the most recent records (overwrite oldest; the default). A 'flush' strategy that writes back to global memory when full is offered as an alternative. All data is copied to global scratch memory at kernel end. On AMD, all lanes write the same slot (a 'collaborative store') to avoid divergence that costs up to 600 cycles.

measurements.what: End-to-end kernel latency overhead with the profiler on
measurements.result: About 8% on average, at most 15% (GEMM software-pipelined with 3 stages, many records)
measurements.workload_gpu: GEMM-SWP-2/3 and FA3 warp-specialized kernels; NVIDIA H100 and AMD MI300X

measurements.what: Shared-memory footprint of the profiling buffer
measurements.result: Production kernels typically leave 1-4 KB of shared memory for the profiling buffer, at most 1.75% of 228 KB on H100. GEMM-SWP-3 leaves 10.9 KB unused. With 4 regions, the circular buffer holds 16 loop iterations. A 512-iteration loop with 2 warp groups and 4 regions would need 4096 slots (16 KB).

systems.not_measured: Circular and flush strategies are described but not compared numerically. No loss count: the circular buffer drops older iterations by design. No scaling with thread count.

systems.system: WarpGuard (Lindenmeier et al., arXiv 2607.13640, 2026) - NVBit-based GPU control-flow tracing on Jetson Orin Nano
systems.design: Design (b) with warp aggregation and per-SM sharding. At each basic-block entry, only the lowest active lane writes (warp_key, addr_id) to its SM's ring buffer. The buffer is in pinned, mapped host memory, so no cudaMemcpy is needed. When a ring fills, the warp flushes it to the CPU-side prover and waits on a doorbell, which can stall it. A flush kernel drains the rest at exit. One CPU receiver thread polls all SM doorbells round-robin. Per-SM sharding 'turned out to be a key improvement to reduce synchronization overhead'. Warp granularity cuts trace volume 'by up to 32x'.

measurements.what: Overhead split: full tracing vs. empty NVBit hook (isolates tracing logic from framework/JIT)
measurements.result: Microbenchmarks (about 281.5K GPU records): the gap between WarpGuard-full and WarpGuard-empty is small. NVBit-empty and DynamoRIO each cause up to about 5x slowdown on their own, and the frameworks account for most of the overhead. Exact values are only in the plot.
measurements.workload_gpu: custom microbenchmarks (FP64 ops per BB, loop iterations, launch count); NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano

measurements.what: End-to-end overhead and the effect of record volume
measurements.result: SPECaccel 2023 with BB-level tracing: 2.4x-128x (mean 39.3x); function-level: 1.2x-113x (mean 26.7x). On md (2.52 billion GPU records), switching to function-level tracing cuts overhead from 9.3x to 1.3x. The authors observe 'thrashing at extremely high GPU record volumes'. On TensorRT models with BB-level tracing: 15.5x-120x. YOLOv3-Tiny (1.2M records/launch) and Super-Res (3.2M records/launch) drop to 0.22 and 0.32 QPS because the CPU drain thread cannot forward ring-buffer records fast enough. This is a measured consumer-side stall symptom.

systems.not_measured: The benefit of per-SM sharding over a single ring is claimed but not quantified. No ring size sweep, stall time or drop count (flushes block instead of dropping). Warp vs. per-thread volume is stated as 'up to 32x', not measured as overhead.

systems.system: BARRACUDA (Eizenberg et al., PLDI 2017, DOI 10.1145/3062341.3062342) - race detector streaming GPU events to the host
systems.design: Design (b) with warp aggregation and multiple queues. Lock-free ring queues of fixed-size records with a write head, commit index and read head. Each record covers one warp operation: warp id, op, 32-bit active mask and 32 addresses, 16 + 8×32 = 272 B. A leader lane reserves the slot, all lanes fill their addresses, and the leader commits with system-level fences. When the queue is full, the leader WAITS for the CPU to drain it, which blocks the warp. Each thread block maps to one queue. Multiple queues give 'orders of magnitude better throughput than a single queue', with about 1.1-1.5 queues per SM found optimal. Each queue has one host thread and one stream.

measurements.what: End-to-end race-detection overhead
measurements.result: Up to 3700x (DWT2D, which runs natively in 90 ms); dxtc takes 20 minutes in absolute time; plotted per benchmark on a log axis
measurements.workload_gpu: Rodinia 3.1, CUB, SHOC, CUDA SDK samples; GTX Titan X (Maxwell, 24 SMs)

comparisons: Darche thesis Ch.5 (MI210, HeCBench, Table 5.2) is the only head-to-head with the instrumentation held fixed. Mean / median kernel slowdown: one global atomic buffer (hip-global-mem) 3.73x / 1.96x; per-CU atomic buffers (hip-cu-mem) 2.47x / 1.60x; global chunk allocator, 4 KiB sub-buffers (hip-chunk-allocator) 1.79x / 1.33x; per-CU chunk allocator 1.77x / 1.32x; exact per-wavefront preallocation from a counting pre-pass (hip-trace) 2.07x / 1.50x, or 2.18x / 1.58x with 4x padding. Source: https://publications.polymtl.ca/67735/1/2025_SebastienDarche.pdf

Darche Fig. 5.7 (MI210 microbenchmark, clock ticks per event). With 256 waves or fewer, global and per-CU atomic buffers cost about 290, chunk about 115, per-CU chunk about 90, exact preallocation about 80 ('almost 3x' cheaper). The single global atomic degrades past 256 waves and peaks at about 750 ticks at 1024 waves. Above about 1024 waves, wave switching hides latency and everything converges to about 300-360 ticks. At 2^18 waves, per-CU atomic (about 320) is slightly ahead of the chunk allocators (about 350-360).

Darche Figs. 5.8-5.10, chunk size: 32 B chunks (one atomic per event) cost about 500 ticks uncontended and about 4600-5000 ticks at 2^12 waves. The benefit levels off at 4 KiB chunks (about 88-113 ticks) and does not improve up to 1 MiB.

Darche Table 6.4 (MI210, HeCBench) medians, full vs. reduced tracepoints: global 2.038 vs 1.822, per-CU 1.871 vs 1.647, chunk 1.477 vs 1.405, per-CU chunk 1.534 vs 1.413, hip-trace 1.709 vs 1.592. Atomic-per-event schemes gain most from lower event rates. Chunk schemes pay a fixed per-wavefront allocation even when few events are emitted. Shared-buffer events carry an extra 32-bit producer id, so their traces are larger.
Darche ECDF (Fig. 5.12): about 75% of kernels stay under 2x with chunk allocators versus about 50-55% with the single global atomic buffer.

PASTA Fig. 9: on-GPU aggregation (design d) vs. a device buffer drained to a single-thread CPU analyzer (design b, NVBit MemTrace or Compute Sanitizer). 941x / 13006x faster on A100, 627x / 7353x on RTX 3060. This mostly reflects where the analysis runs, not buffer allocation (Fig. 10 shows CPU variants are dominated by analysis time).

iGUARD vs. BARRACUDA: in-GPU race detection (design d) at 5.1x average vs. Barracuda's host-queue design (b, per-warp 272 B records, blocking when full) at over 50x, about 15x lower overhead. Barracuda also reserves 50% of GPU memory for its queues. Numbers come from iGUARD's paper, and the comparison mixes in different detection algorithms.
notes:
Scope covered: hip-analyzer / Darche (TOPC 2024 article plus the 2025 PhD thesis, which contains the follow-up buffer-design article, Ch. 5, submitted to TOPC on 2024-11-18 and not yet found published), PASTA, CUDAAdvisor, GPA, GPUscout, plus three other tracing systems found in the literature search with relevant buffer designs (KPerfIR/Proton, WarpGuard, BARRACUDA, with iGUARD as a third-party measurement). NVBit, SASSI, GT-Pin, Neutrino, Xtrace, gpu_ext and the CUPTI internals were deliberately left to other workflow steps.

Key takeaways for bpftime direction 1:
(1) The only study that measures buffer designs head-to-head is Darche Ch. 5, and it is AMD-only (MI210), with one producer per 64-thread wavefront and 24 B events. It ranks the designs: wave-level chunk reservation (one atomic per 4 KiB) beats per-CU atomics, which beat one global atomic per event. The gap is largest when contention is high but the hardware is not yet oversubscribed (256 to about 4096 waves). Mean slowdown drops from 3.73x to about 1.78x on HeCBench.
(2) Nobody in this group measures drop/overwrite rates, the time spent blocked when a buffer is full, or a memory-footprint comparison between designs. Darche explicitly leaves fragmentation and memory cost unexplored. His Table 4.4 memory ratios (up to 8279x) include input duplication.
(3) Per-thread producers (bpftime's current per-thread-index layout) are never measured in this group. Darche mentions the per-thread mode only qualitatively as 'large overhead both for memory usage and execution time'.
(4) On NVIDIA, the host cannot read device memory consistently during a kernel on discrete AMD (CDNA2), which forces flight-recorder or overwrite semantics. WarpGuard and BARRACUDA instead use pinned or host-mapped queues with blocking flushes, and WarpGuard shows the CPU drain thread becomes the bottleneck at more than 1M records per launch, on a Jetson Orin Nano, the same platform family as this board.

Caveats: values from Figs. 5.7-5.12 were read off rendered plots (pages 70-75 of the thesis PDF) and are approximate. Table 5.2 and Table 6.4 report different medians for the same methods because they are separate runs. The CUDAAdvisor PDF could not be opened (ACM 403), so its 10x-120x (~50x Rodinia) overhead is secondhand via Darche. Its repo facts (a ~1.97 GB global buffer, one atomicAdd per event, silent drop when full) were verified directly in the code: common.h L1, src/ansf.cu L623-634 and L690-695. GPA and GPUscout publish no collection-overhead numbers. (2) The bpftime per-thread host-mapped ring is the dominant cost of kernelretsnoop: about 91% loss compact, about 99% full-record. (4) The 1024-thread default silently skips threads beyond slot 1024; official bpftime instead writes past the map for the per-thread array. Upstream micro rows at large/xlarge are invalid (faster than baseline).
(5) No source measures drops under real overflow on the GPU. Every GPU campaign reports 0 drops because capacity was oversized. The only GPU data loss measured is the official host drain losing 75% of events on Orin.

CUPTI PC sampling is blocking/serializing: 'NVIDIA's PC sampling measurement serializes execution of GPU kernels ... slows the execution of applications' (HPCToolkit arXiv 2109.06931 Sec. 9), and 'PC Sampling with NVIDIA's CUPTI serializes kernel executions', so concurrent-kernel effects cannot be measured (GPA arXiv 2009.04061, conclusion). This is a qualitative statement with no number. GPA Sec. 2: each SM collects samples individually; when an SM's buffer is full, CUPTI merges the samples from all SMs and transfers them to the CPU.

GVProf: 'GPU memory overhead of GVProf is bounded by the size of the GPU queue, [while] the runtime overhead is proportional to the number of instrumentation callbacks invoked' (SC'20 Sec. IV-A(c)). This is a stated footprint bound, not a measured peak. Default block sampling period 50 was chosen from sweeps over periods 2,3,4,8,10,16,32,50,64,100 (Sec. V-B(b)); only the 50 results are tabulated. Fig. 6: strong scaling of LAMMPS to 64 GPUs on 11 Summit nodes. Block-sampling overhead falls as GPUs are added; kernel-sampling overhead rises from 1 to several GPUs and converges with block sampling at 64 (Sec. V-D). Values are in the figure only. Mechanism detail: it intercepts the launch, locks the stream, and a priority stream repeatedly polls whether the queue is full, then copies, clears and resumes (Sec. IV-A(b)).

Neutrino (OSDI'25 preprint, design (a), maps sized from blockDim/gridDim, Sec. 3.3), Table 3 kernel slowdown (A100 80GB / RTX 4090 testbed; the table does not say which GPU each row used). Lightweight probes average 1.04x (block_sched warp:array:16:1, gmem_bytes thread:array:8:1, tensorop_count; range 0.96x-1.39x, max 1.3882x for gmem_bytes on Max/AvgPool). Per-thread mem_trace probe (thread:array:16:count) 2.75x (Conv2D) to 13.16x (SoftMax); the paper calls the dmat probe 7.12x on average and blames its frequent memory I/O (App. I). Extra registers: 3.78 (light) / 5.09 (dmat); Group-GEMM mem_trace spills +516 registers. Fig. 12 measures peak GMEM probe memory in whole-model forward passes (ResNet, Stable Diffusion, Mamba-1.7B, Llama3-1/3/8B). Light probes use at least 10x less than the model's own memory; dmat mostly stays within the original usage at batch 256; the probe share shrinks as the model grows (Sec. 6.3). This is the only measured footprint of a grid-sized design among these sources. End-to-end only, no buffer-vs-probe split.

Darche & Dagenais (ACM TOPC 2024, doi 10.1145/3649510; seen only through the authors' slides sdarche_may2024/dec2023/dSebastien_dec2024). Two-pass LLVM instrumentation: a counter run, then a trace run with buffers pre-allocated from the known control flow (a variant of design (a)). Rodinia averages/medians: counter kernels 2.00x/1.67x, tracing kernels 1.50x/1.29x, program time 1.60x/1.26x. The slides name no GPU (AMD GCN/CDNA figures shown) and cite prior tools at ~10-120x and ~1-151x (avg 13.2x). Three runtime-buffer variants are implemented but unmeasured in the slides: one shared global buffer ('heavy use of atomics'), a global circular buffer allocated in fixed-size chunks, and per-CU circular buffers. The paper PDF itself was not obtained (3649510.pdf is a 5 KB stub).

GT-Pin docs, confirmed by fetch: GtProfileArray groups threads into buckets 'to minimize contention of concurrent memory accesses'; bucket count in [1, max HW threads], rounded up to a power of two, thread ID hashed to a bucket; the page says nothing about overflow. GtProfileTrace: maxTraceSize in bytes, maxThreads default 0x1000 = 'maximum number of threads concurrently accessing the trace'; IsTruncated() true when the trace 'has been trimmed to avoid buffer overflow'; the generated code sets f0.0 when a record cannot be allocated.
